predecessors.name: Kingdom of Kush
predecessors.text: the Gezira, the Butana and Meroë: 'Meroë was then taken by the Kingdom of Alodia' (Meroë page)

successors.name: Funj Sultanate
successors.text: Soba and the Gezira: 'In 1504-1505 the Funj founded the Funj sultanate, incorporating Abdallah Jammah's domain'

successors.name: Kingdom of Fazughli
successors.text: the mountains of Fazughli in the Ethiopian-Sudanese borderlands, where the Alodian remnant 'gradually retreated ... forming the Kingdom of Fazughli'

ledger.x: 347: Alwa rises in the Gezira after Kush.

c. 950: Alodia at its widest. 'A century later, in the mid-10th century, Alodia was visited by traveler and historian Ibn Hawqal'; al-Aswani found it 'more powerful than Makuria, more extensive and having a larger army'; Eusebios reigned c. 938-955; 'a vassal king loyal to Alodia governed the region around the Gash…
By 1276: al-Abwab is an independent kingdom.
By December 1365: the Red Sea reach is Banu Kanz land.
By 1450: Alodia shrinks to the Soba-Gezira core.
1504: the Funj and Abdallah Jammah end Alwa.

wars.name: Fall of Alodia (Abdallab and Funj)
wars.outcome: Soba attacked in 1474 and, by the Shendi tradition, 'destroyed by Abdallah Jammah in 1509'; the Funj 'attacked and defeated the kingdom of the Nuba in 1504-1505' and founded their sultanate 'incorporating Abdallah Jammah's domain'.

certainty.note: Every frontier approximate: the Makurian frontier near Abu Hamad/al-Abwab, the Kordofan and Red Sea Hills edges and the Ethiopian border ('it is likely that it bordered the Ethiopian highlands') are readings of 10th-century travellers.
